paragraphs: This paper asks how a vision-language model can selectively lose recognition ability for a visual domain while retaining it elsewhere. The distinction is more specific than forgetting an object category. For example, a system might need to recognize real cars while avoiding treating illustrated cars in advertisements as real vehicles.

The authors introduce Approximate Domain Unlearning to formalize this goal. Its central difficulty comes from a strength of pretrained models: their representations connect objects across domains so effectively that the domains become intertwined. Simply penalizing recognition on the domain to be forgotten is therefore ineffective in the setting described. The proposed method explicitly separates domain distributions and adapts to domain information associated with individual examples.

Experiments on four datasets containing multiple domains show significant improvements over strong baselines based on existing vision-language model tuning techniques. These findings support finer control over which domains a model recognizes. The contribution concerns approximate, selective changes in recognition behavior rather than a demonstrated guarantee that every trace of domain knowledge has been erased.
neurips-2025-approximate-domain-unlearni.tldr: The paper introduces a method for selectively reducing a vision-language model’s recognition of specified domains while preserving recognition elsewhere.

paragraphs: BO4Mob turns an urban transportation problem into a benchmark for optimization methods: estimating how much travel occurs between different origins and destinations using limited traffic sensor observations. This is an inverse problem because the desired travel demand must be inferred from its effects on the road network, rather than observed directly.

The benchmark contains five scenarios built around real road networks in San Jose, California, with as many as 10,100 input dimensions. High-resolution, open-source traffic simulations provide realistic nonlinear and stochastic behavior. Each candidate evaluation is computationally expensive, can vary because of randomness, and does not supply derivatives. Together, these properties make the scenarios challenging tests for Bayesian optimization at large scale.

The authors demonstrate the framework by evaluating three state-of-the-art Bayesian optimization algorithms and two other optimization baselines. The contribution is a realistic testing environment, with no particular winner stated in the abstract. It is intended to support scalable optimization research and transportation modeling, including detailed digital representations of metropolitan road networks.
neurips-2025-bo4mob-bayesian-optimizatio.tldr: BO4Mob provides five realistic traffic-demand estimation scenarios for testing optimization methods in spaces with up to 10,100 dimensions.

paragraphs: The Continuous Thought Machine explores an architecture in which the timing of neural activity is central to computation. Inspired by biological neural dynamics, it gives individual artificial neurons richer processing behavior while aiming to remain computationally manageable. The work presents this architectural direction rather than pursuing new state-of-the-art benchmark results.

Two mechanisms define the model. Each neuron has its own parameters for processing a history of incoming signals, making its response depend on activity over time. The model then uses synchronization between neurons as an internal representation. Together, these mechanisms make temporal relationships part of how information is represented and processed, rather than treating neurons only as immediate transformations of their inputs.

The authors demonstrate the model on tasks including two-dimensional maze solving, ImageNet-1K classification, and parity computation. They report capabilities for complex sequential reasoning and internal processes that offer opportunities for interpretation. The model also supports adaptive computation: it can finish earlier on simpler instances or continue processing harder ones. These demonstrations establish versatility for the proposed design without claiming benchmark leadership.
neurips-2025-continuous-thought-machines.tldr: Continuous Thought Machines use neuron-specific temporal processing and neural synchronization to support sequential reasoning and adaptive computation.

paragraphs: This paper connects learning probability distributions with algorithms for counting and sampling graph structures. Through an online learning framework, it brings tools from graph algorithms into the task of learning high-dimensional graphical models. Its main result concerns Bayesian networks whose underlying undirected graph, or skeleton, is supplied and chordal.

The algorithm receives samples from a distribution over n variables, each with k possible values, together with the graph and an indegree parameter d. It returns a Bayesian network whose Kullback–Leibler divergence from the sampled distribution is at most epsilon above the best achievable within the specified network family. This covers both realizable cases, where the target belongs to that family, and agnostic cases, where it may not.

The stated sample requirement is approximately n³k^(d+1)/epsilon², suppressing logarithmic factors, and runtime is polynomial in n, k, and inverse epsilon when d is constant. That qualification matters to the efficiency claim. The result extends earlier guarantees centered on tree skeletons, and the paper also establishes additional results for tree and polytree distributions.
neurips-2025-distribution-learning-meets.tldr: Graph-structure sampling enables an efficient algorithm for learning Bayesian networks with a given chordal skeleton when indegree is constant.

paragraphs: Learning continuously from unlabeled examples creates two connected problems: the model needs useful training targets, and new learning can overwrite earlier knowledge. Existing approaches often construct artificial labels by clustering visual representations. The paper argues that noise and poor quality in these labels can undermine the model’s subsequent development.

The proposed method combines visual information with language descriptions. A large multimodal model first describes a small set of representative examples. A coarse-to-fine refinement process then makes those descriptions more sensitive to differences between data points. The refined text is combined with visual features to generate hybrid pseudo labels, giving the learner supervision informed by both appearance and semantic description.

The descriptions also support semantic alignment distillation, which uses the stability of language knowledge to alleviate forgetting as the stream continues. Language therefore contributes both to learning new distinctions and to preserving earlier information. Experiments across several benchmarks report state-of-the-art performance, while ablation studies support the effectiveness of the proposed method’s components.
neurips-2025-dual-space-semantic-synergy.tldr: The method combines refined text descriptions with visual features to improve unlabeled continual learning and alleviate forgetting.

paragraphs: Contrastive learning often teaches a model to recognize different augmented versions of the same example as semantically equivalent. The paper questions whether that training signal is always appropriate. Strong transformations can change meaningful content or distort it, so demanding the same similarity for every pair of views can give the model a misleading objective.

Contrastive Learning with Variable Similarity, or CLVS, makes the desired similarity depend on augmentation strength. Strongly augmented views are always assigned lower similarity scores than weakly augmented views. This changes the supervision from a uniform assumption of semantic invariance to a graded relationship that reflects how extensively the input was altered.

The authors provide a theoretical analysis supporting improved generalizability from variable similarity. Their experiments report gains of 2.1% on ImageNet-100 and 1.4% on ImageNet-1k over state-of-the-art methods. These findings support adjusting how closely augmented views should match, especially when the transformations used for training can introduce semantic discrepancies. The key contribution is a more differentiated training target for learning representations.
neurips-2025-enhancing-contrastive-learn.tldr: CLVS improves contrastive learning by assigning lower target similarity to more strongly augmented views.

paragraphs: This paper develops an optimization method that generalizes gradient norm clipping beyond Euclidean geometry. Its design combines steepest descent and conditional gradient approaches. The aim is to connect these update strategies through a shared mathematical framework, with a descent property established under a generalized form of (L0, L1)-smoothness.

That smoothness condition supplies the setting for the descent guarantee: the result is tied to the stated mathematical assumption. The paper also gives weight decay a principled role by relating it to the Frank-Wolfe short step. This connection places weight decay within the structure of the optimization method rather than presenting it only as an additional tuning choice.

For stochastic optimization, the authors use a momentum-based gradient estimator and prove an order-optimal O(n^(-1/4)) convergence rate. They also describe deep learning versions of the algorithms, named Clipped Scion, and demonstrate their properties on image classification and language modeling. The contribution combines theoretical guarantees with practical instantiations, showing how the generalized clipping framework can be used in neural network training.
neurips-2025-generalized-gradient-norm-c.tldr: Clipped Scion generalizes gradient clipping through non-Euclidean optimization, with descent and stochastic convergence guarantees under the stated framework.

paragraphs: Retrieval-augmented image generation uses reference images to improve generated output, creating a need to detect unauthorized use of private image collections. Ordinary digital watermarks face a specific obstacle here: feature extraction and recombination during generation can fail to preserve the watermark signal. ImageSentinel addresses verification in this setting.

The framework synthesizes sentinel images that visually fit the dataset they accompany. It uses vision-language models to create these images, helping them integrate with the original collection. Randomly generated character sequences serve as retrieval keys for protection verification. The proposed mechanism therefore combines specially generated visual content with a way to retrieve that content when checking dataset usage.

Experiments show that ImageSentinel can detect unauthorized dataset use while preserving generation quality for authorized applications. This pairing matters because the protection mechanism is intended to coexist with useful image generation. The stated contribution is a verification framework for detecting use, with evidence that its sentinel-based approach can remain effective in the retrieval-augmented generation setting.
neurips-2025-imagesentinel-protecting-vi.tldr: ImageSentinel uses visually consistent sentinel images and random-character retrieval keys to detect unauthorized use of image datasets.

paragraphs: LinPrim explores how the basic building blocks of a three-dimensional scene affect reconstruction and rendering. Modern novel-view synthesis methods optimize scene representations from observed images using differentiable rendering. This paper investigates an alternative to representations based on neural radiance fields or three-dimensional Gaussians.

The authors introduce two representations built from octahedra and tetrahedra. Each primitive is a homogeneous volume enclosed by triangular faces, giving the scene a collection of transparent polyhedral building blocks. A GPU-efficient differentiable rasterizer allows gradients from rendered images to optimize these primitives end to end, while retaining the ability to render in real time.

Experiments on real-world datasets report performance comparable to state-of-the-art volumetric methods, using fewer primitives for similar reconstruction fidelity. The finding concerns how much representational work each primitive can do, alongside rendering performance. More broadly, the results show that transparent polyhedra are a useful option in the design of learned three-dimensional representations and expand the set of primitives available for differentiable volumetric rendering.
neurips-2025-linprim-linear-primitives-f.tldr: LinPrim represents scenes with differentiable octahedral and tetrahedral volumes, achieving comparable reconstruction quality with fewer primitives.

paragraphs: Neural Entropy studies diffusion models through an information-theoretic question: how much information does a trained neural network store about the structure it generates? Diffusion removes information as data becomes noise. Generation runs in the opposite direction, imperfectly restoring information through knowledge stored in the model during training.

The paper introduces neural entropy as a measure of this stored information and relates it to the total entropy produced by diffusion. A central feature is that the measure depends on both the data distribution and the diffusion process. Consequently, its interpretation involves how information is erased and restored, as well as the collection of examples being modeled.

Measurements on a few simple image diffusion models indicate that they compress large ensembles of structured data extremely efficiently. The empirical claim is specifically grounded in those models. The contribution provides a way to quantify the information involved in diffusion-based learning and generation, connecting the network’s learned representation to the information loss of the process it learns to reverse.
neurips-2025-neural-entropy-1089f7f65a.tldr: Neural entropy quantifies information stored by diffusion models, with measurements on simple image models indicating highly efficient compression.

paragraphs: Influence estimates help identify which training examples matter to a model, but computing them with large language models can be expensive. Repeated forward and backward passes and substantial memory requirements limit scalability. Existing approaches can also struggle to generalize influence estimates to new data.

The paper proposes InfluenceNetwork, a small neural network trained to estimate influence values. Its broader algorithm, NN-CIFT, applies these estimates to selecting subsets of data for instruction fine-tuning. The central idea is to learn an efficient estimator of influence so that data selection can benefit from influence information without repeatedly paying the full computational cost of the original methods.

Across the evaluated language models, ranging from 1.5 billion to 22 billion parameters, the influence estimators average just 0.0007% of the full models’ size. The authors report cost reductions of up to 99%. In comparisons involving four state-of-the-art influence functions, subset selection with NN-CIFT shows no performance compromise relative to the original functions despite substantial speedups. The paper also examines how hyperparameters affect the method.
neurips-2025-neural-networks-for-learnab.tldr: NN-CIFT learns influence estimates with tiny neural networks, reducing costs by up to 99% without sacrificing evaluated data-selection performance.

paragraphs: OmniTalker generates synchronized speech and talking video from text while imitating a target identity’s speaking and facial movement styles. These styles include speech characteristics, head motion, and facial dynamics. The paper focuses on jointly producing both modalities in a one-shot framework, addressing a less explored setting than audio-driven talking-head generation.

Its diffusion transformer has separate audio and video branches. Early layers exchange information through cross-modal fusion modules, while deeper layers process each modality independently. A vocoder decodes the audio, and a GAN-based renderer produces the visual output. A masked-infilling strategy uses the transformer’s in-context learning ability to capture audio and visual styles without explicit style-extraction modules.

The authors report real-time inference at 25 frames per second, supported by the backbone and optimized renderer. Experiments show advantages over existing methods in generation quality, particularly style consistency and audio-video synchronization. The authors also describe OmniTalker, to their knowledge, as the first one-shot framework to jointly model speech and facial styles in real time.
neurips-2025-omnitalker-one-shot-real-ti.tldr: OmniTalker jointly generates speech and talking video from text, mimicking audio and facial styles at a reported 25 frames per second.

paragraphs: A graph convolutional neural network uses both node information and the connections between nodes. Its stability concerns how much its output changes when the graph structure changes slightly. This paper develops a formulation for studying that sensitivity while accounting for the statistical properties of the data carried by the nodes.

The approach moves beyond analyses focused only on worst-case perturbations. It characterizes output changes across a broad range of input data, creating a probabilistic account of how node-data distributions interact with changes in graph topology. This makes the data distribution an explicit part of the stability analysis, rather than considering structural perturbations in isolation.

The authors validate their theoretical findings experimentally and report benefits over existing baselines in representation stability and adversarial attacks on downstream tasks. These results support the practical value of the distribution-aware formulation. The central contribution is a way to reason about graph-network sensitivity that connects the graph’s changing structure with the statistical characteristics of the information being processed.
neurips-2025-on-the-stability-of-graph-c.tldr: The paper analyzes graph-network stability probabilistically by accounting for how node-data distributions interact with structural perturbations.

paragraphs: State estimation aims to recover a dynamical system’s hidden state from noisy observations. LLM-Filter explores whether knowledge inside a pretrained language model can help with this task. It maps noisy observations into a representation aligned with text prototypes, allowing a frozen language model to participate in the estimation process.

The framework also introduces System-as-Prompt, a prompt structure containing instructions about the task and the particular system. These prompts guide adaptation across systems. The combination matters because the model must both receive observations in a compatible form and understand the estimation task those observations are meant to support.

In experiments on classical dynamical systems, proper modality alignment enables LLM-Filter to outperform state-of-the-art learning-based approaches. The authors also report accurate filtering in changed and previously unseen environments, together with a scaling pattern in which larger models and longer training improve accuracy. These findings motivate its proposed role as a foundation model for filtering, with the evidence coming from the systems and conditions evaluated.
neurips-2025-one-filters-all-a-generalis.tldr: LLM-Filter aligns noisy observations with a frozen language model and uses system-specific prompts to estimate hidden dynamical states.

paragraphs: Shapley values and related probabilistic values assign contributions to features or data, making them useful for explaining models and valuing training examples. Exact computation takes exponential time, so practical methods rely on approximations. This paper develops a new combination of Monte Carlo sampling and regression-based estimation.

Its main flexibility is that the regression component can use any function family whose probabilistic values are efficiently computable. This permits models such as XGBoost to contribute their predictive accuracy while the resulting estimates remain unbiased. The condition on efficient value computation is important: it defines which function families can be used within the approach.

Experiments on eight datasets report state-of-the-art estimation performance. For Shapley values, errors are up to six times lower than Permutation SHAP, 2.75 times lower than Kernel SHAP, and 1.75 times lower than Leverage SHAP. For more general probabilistic values, the reported reduction reaches a factor of 60. These are maximum observed improvements, demonstrating the potential benefit of combining flexible fitted models with unbiased sampling-based estimation.
neurips-2025-regression-adjusted-monte-c.tldr: The method combines Monte Carlo sampling with flexible regression models to produce unbiased, more accurate estimates of probabilistic contribution values.

paragraphs: Retrieving relevant evidence does not by itself ensure that a language model reasons consistently with it. This paper calls the resulting divergence reasoning misalignment and treats retrieval-augmented generation as a problem of evidence-constrained reasoning. AlignRAG addresses that problem through iterative critique and refinement at test time.

The framework trains a dedicated critic language model using labeled critiques that distinguish evidence-aligned reasoning from misaligned reasoning. Its contrastive critique synthesis mechanism is designed to make feedback sensitive to retrieval while reducing self-bias. An autonomous version, AlignRAG-auto, decides when to stop refinement, removing the need to choose a fixed number of critique rounds beforehand.

The authors report that their eight-billion-parameter critic improves performance over Self-Refine by 12.1% on out-of-domain tasks and exceeds a standard 72-billion-parameter critic by 2.2%. The autonomous variant retains the reported state-of-the-art performance while choosing its refinement length dynamically. Experiments also indicate robustness with informative and noisy retrieval. Designed as an add-on to existing RAG architectures, the framework strengthens the connection between evidence and reasoning.
neurips-2025-retrieval-is-not-enough-enh.tldr: AlignRAG uses a trained retrieval-aware critic to iteratively improve reasoning consistency with evidence and can automatically decide when to stop.

paragraphs: Robo2VLM explores how robot experience can improve vision-language models. Robot demonstrations contain information beyond images and descriptions, including end-effector pose, gripper opening, and force measurements. The framework uses these sensory signals to derive ground truth for visual question answering, connecting questions about visible interactions to recorded physical information.

Starting with a human-operated robot demonstration, Robo2VLM divides the trajectory into manipulation phases. For each phase, it identifies properties of the robot, task goal, and target object using scene and interaction understanding. These properties feed templates that generate image-based multiple-choice questions about spatial relationships, goals, and interactions.

Using a subset of Open X-Embodiment, the authors construct Robo2VLM-1 with 684,710 questions from 176,000 real robot trajectories. The collection spans 463 scenes and 3,396 manipulation tasks. Results suggest that this dataset can both evaluate and improve spatial and interaction reasoning in vision-language models. The contribution is a route from rich robot sensor records to large-scale question-answering supervision grounded in real manipulation.
neurips-2025-robo2vlm-improving-visual-q.tldr: Robo2VLM converts robot demonstrations and sensor measurements into visual questions for evaluating and improving spatial and interaction reasoning.

paragraphs: RoPECraft transfers motion from a reference video into video generation without training the diffusion transformer. It operates by modifying rotary positional embeddings, or RoPE, which provide positional information within the model. The approach makes those embeddings the mechanism for injecting and refining the reference motion during generation.

First, dense optical flow estimates motion across the reference video. The resulting offsets warp the complex-valued tensors used by RoPE, encoding that motion into the generation process. During denoising, the method further optimizes the embeddings through a flow-matching objective that aligns predicted and target velocities along trajectories. Thus, being training-free still involves optimization while producing the output.

A regularization term based on the reference video’s Fourier phase information helps preserve agreement with the text prompt and prevent duplicate generations. Smoothing the phase angles is used to suppress high-frequency artifacts. Benchmark experiments report qualitative and quantitative improvements over all recently published methods considered. The contribution demonstrates motion control through positional embeddings, supported by trajectory alignment and phase-based regularization.
neurips-2025-ropecraft-training-free-mot.tldr: RoPECraft transfers reference-video motion by modifying and optimizing a diffusion transformer’s rotary positional embeddings during generation.

paragraphs: STaRFormer is motivated by predicting the intentions of smart-device users near vehicles from sequences of spatial and temporal observations. Real sensor data complicates this task: its statistical behavior can change over time, and observations can arrive at irregular intervals. The paper develops a broader sequential-modeling approach around these challenges.

The Transformer-based model combines dynamic attention-based regional masking with semi-supervised contrastive learning. Masking and contrastive learning are used together to improve internal representations for the task being solved. This emphasis on task-informed representations links the training approach to the eventual prediction goal, including intent prediction in the motivating application.

The evaluation covers 56 datasets spanning different tasks, domains, sequence lengths, training-set sizes, and applications, including non-stationary and irregularly sampled data. The authors report notable improvements over state-of-the-art approaches across this broad experimental study. These results support STaRFormer’s usefulness as a general sequential-modeling framework, with evidence extending beyond the vehicle-related scenario that originally motivated its design.
neurips-2025-starformer-semi-supervised-.tldr: STaRFormer combines attention-based masking and semi-supervised contrastive learning to improve sequential representations across varied datasets.

paragraphs: Trajectory modeling includes finding patterns in movement data and predicting future movement. Many specialized methods exist, but differences between datasets and tasks make effective modeling difficult even for experts. TrajAgent uses language-model agents to automate this work while drawing on smaller models specialized for trajectory tasks.

The framework begins with UniEnv, an execution environment that provides a common interface for data and models. This supports training and running different specialized models within one workflow. An agentic process built on that environment automates trajectory modeling across tasks and datasets. The authors also introduce collaborative learning between the language-model agents and specialized models to improve the overall system.

Experiments cover four tasks using four real-world datasets and report improvements ranging from 2.38% to 69.91% over baseline methods. The range reflects results across the evaluated settings. The contribution is an integrated approach to coordinating diverse modeling tools, using language-model agents alongside specialized predictors to make trajectory analysis more automated and effective.
neurips-2025-trajagent-an-llm-agent-fram.tldr: TrajAgent automates trajectory modeling through a shared execution environment and collaboration between language-model agents and specialized models.

paragraphs: Vehicle GPS traces contain both movement patterns and clues about travel purpose. Learning those meanings efficiently is difficult because road functions and points of interest are described in text, while raw trajectories can contain many redundant points. TrajMamba addresses both the semantic modeling cost and the cost of processing unnecessary observations.

Its Traj-Mamba Encoder jointly models trajectories from GPS and road perspectives to represent continuous travel behavior. A travel-purpose-aware pretraining procedure incorporates purpose information into the resulting embeddings without adding overhead to embedding calculation. This places the work of learning travel semantics in pretraining while keeping the later representation calculation efficient.

A further knowledge-distillation pretraining scheme uses a learnable mask generator to identify important trajectory points and produce compressed embeddings. This connects reducing redundancy with preserving useful representations. Experiments on two real-world datasets and three downstream tasks report improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in both efficiency and accuracy. The findings support combining movement modeling, purpose-aware learning, and learned trajectory compression within one pretrained model.
neurips-2025-trajmamba-an-efficient-and-.tldr: TrajMamba combines GPS and road modeling, purpose-aware pretraining, and learned trajectory compression to improve accuracy and efficiency.

paragraphs: In-context learning lets a language model use examples in its prompt to perform a task. Previous explanations have often focused separately on particular attention heads or task vectors at selected layers. This paper connects these components by examining how the model’s internal query representations evolve across layers during classification tasks.

The proposed framework centers on two geometric properties: separability and alignment. The layer-by-layer analysis reveals a two-stage pattern, with separability emerging early and alignment developing later. This gives an account of how changes in hidden-state geometry relate to performance across the model’s depth, bringing previously separate mechanisms into a shared description.

Ablation studies associate Previous Token Heads with driving separability, while Induction Heads and task vectors improve alignment. These findings assign different roles to the components within the same overall process. The resulting explanation links attention heads, task vectors, and hidden-state evolution for the classification setting studied, offering a unified account of how these internal mechanisms contribute to in-context learning.
neurips-2025-unifying-attention-heads-an.tldr: The paper links attention heads and task vectors through a two-stage pattern of early separability and later alignment in classification representations.

paragraphs: This paper explores which different inputs a Transformer treats as equivalent. Equivalence is defined through the model’s output: inputs belong to the same class when they produce the same probability distribution over predicted classes. The aim is to navigate input space according to the distinctions the model actually makes.

The mathematical framework treats successive Transformer layers as deformations of an input manifold. It takes a distance metric defined at the output and maps it back through the model’s Jacobian, which describes sensitivity to input changes. An eigendecomposition of this pulled-back metric enables the method to reconstruct and move across equivalence classes in input space.

The framework supports two complementary procedures. One finds inputs that preserve the original class-probability distribution; the other finds inputs that produce a different distribution. The authors also show how to project the resulting embeddings into a human-readable form. Together, these operations make it possible to inspect both variations the model treats alike and changes that alter its classification behavior.
neurips-2025-unveiling-transformer-perce.tldr: The method uses Transformer geometry to find interpretable input variations that preserve or change the model’s output probability distribution.

paragraphs: VideoUFO addresses a mismatch between the videos used to train text-to-video models and the topics people actually request. A model may perform unevenly because its training material does not cover some desired subjects. The dataset therefore starts from real user prompts to guide which videos are collected.

The authors cluster the million-scale VidProM prompt collection into 1,291 user-focused topics. They retrieve Creative Commons videos through YouTube’s official API, divide them into clips, generate short and detailed captions, and verify topic relevance. The resulting collection contains over 1.09 million clips and has a reported overlap of only 0.29% with existing video datasets.

Tests of 16 text-to-video models reveal inconsistent performance across the user-focused topics. A simple model trained on VideoUFO outperforms other models on the worst-performing topics in the experiments. These findings support the value of choosing training data around observed user interests, particularly for topics existing systems handle poorly. The paper contributes both a large captioned video collection and evidence connecting topic coverage to generation performance.
neurips-2025-videoufo-a-million-scale-us.tldr: VideoUFO collects over 1.09 million captioned clips around real user interests to improve coverage of difficult text-to-video topics.

paragraphs: This paper builds an automated pipeline for collecting animal video data from YouTube and preparing it for animal-centered vision tasks. The pipeline produces object-centric clips and auxiliary annotations for applications including pose estimation, tracking, and three-dimensional reconstruction over time. It collects 30,000 videos containing two million frames, an order of magnitude more than prior work.

To study reconstruction of moving quadrupeds, the authors introduce Animal4D: 230 manually filtered sequences with 11,000 frames showing clean, varied animal motion. Evaluations reveal a mismatch between numerical scores and three-dimensional plausibility. Two-dimensional metrics favor model-based methods even when their reconstructed shapes look unrealistic, while model-free methods produce more natural reconstructions but receive lower scores.

The authors also extend a recent model-free approach with sequence-level optimization, establishing a baseline for four-dimensional animal reconstruction. The combined contribution includes data collection, a benchmark, and a reconstruction method. The evaluation finding is particularly consequential: better agreement under two-dimensional metrics does not necessarily correspond to more natural three-dimensional animal shape in the tested methods.
neurips-2025-web-scale-collection-of-vid.tldr: The paper provides large-scale animal video collection, an Animal4D benchmark, and a reconstruction baseline while exposing a mismatch in existing evaluation metrics.
